name: Never Hear the End of It

podcast.body: Described as a "30 song, Opus," this album was recorded by the band in their own practice space, showcasing their self-sufficiency in production. Learning all 30 songs for subsequent touring proved to be a significant challenge for the band members, highlighting the extensive nature of the work. "Never hear the end of it. The 30 song, Opus."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Sloan In Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.body: This eighth album by Sloan featured an ambitious 30 songs and over 76 minutes of music spread across two discs. The band considered the sheer volume of songs a "hook" that helped the album perform well and receive positive write-ups. Chris Murphy noted that 14 of the 30 songs were his, making it feel "like a solo record of mine hidden within its low record." "Our eighth record has 30 songs on it. We didn't need 30 new songs in our set."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
